changeSet.author: nexus-ykzbj.8
changeSet.comment: SELECT-only grants for the nexus_diag diagnostic role (RDR-182 P2.1). LEGACY-era: applies only while nexus.diag_chash_conformance is absent — the era test is the second guard in the body below, NOT a preCondition (nexus-ixsxa; see the header note on MARK_RAN row growth). Conditional on the role existing (clean skip otherwise; self-heals every startup via runAlways). ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES runs as this migration connection's role (nexus_admin — the creator of every schema table), so future tables are covered automatically. Read-only by construction: SELECT on tables plus the Liquibase journal; deliberately NO sequence usage, NO DML, NO EXECUTE on the soft-delete functions.

changeSet.author: nexus-9bufb
changeSet.comment: Amendment A6 (nexus-9bufb): VIEW-era grants. Once the superuser provisioning path has created nexus.diag_chash_conformance, the diagnostic role's content boundary becomes structural: revoke direct table SELECT (nexus_admin owns the tables and made the original grants, so it can revoke them), keep schema USAGE, the counts view, and the Liquibase journal. Idempotent + runAlways: self-heals every boot, and re-revokes anything the legacy changeset era granted. The era test is the second guard in the body below, NOT a preCondition (nexus-ixsxa; see the header note on MARK_RAN row growth).

changeSet.author: nexus-8yz1p
changeSet.comment:
bead nexus-8yz1p (2026-08-16): nexus_diag gets staging schema SELECT, ERA-INDEPENDENT. Deliberately its OWN changeset rather than folded into grants-nexus-diag-1's body: the LEGACY/VIEW split above is specifically the RDR-182 s5 chash-poison content boundary on nexus/t1 -- staging (the RDR-180 land-then-transform landing zone, FORCE RLS + tenant policy on every table, staging-001-landing-tables.xml) carries no such content-boundary concern and no counts view to narrow into, so it must grant identically in both eras. A single-changeset placement would force an impossible choice: before diag-1's era guard, and it trips ChangelogBulkGrantConformanceTest's allowlistedOccurrence_isStillGatedByViewAbsence tripwire (which asserts the FIRST bulk "ON ALL TABLES" grant found in grants-nexus-diag-1's body sits after the era guard -- a sound invariant for the nexus/t1 grant it was written to protect, but not one this era-independent grant should be measured against); after the guard, and it would be silently skipped in the view era, defeating the whole point. A separate changeset id sidesteps the tripwire's substring scan entirely (which slices ONLY id="grants-nexus-diag-1"'s body) without editing that test's assertion, and reads as the more honest shape besides: this grant is not part of the era dance at all. Same role-existence guard as -1/-2 (self-heals every boot); read-only by construction, matching -1's own construction.
EXTENDED (2026-08-17, bead nexus-lhuhe, P1) — closes a THIRD grants-era interaction bug this file's own -1/-2 sequencing created against taxonomy-011-8 (taxonomy-011-doc-id-bytea.xml). taxonomy-011-8 creates nexus.diag_chash_conformance (WITH security_invoker=true) and grants nexus_diag SELECT on it, every boot — but taxonomy-011-doc-id-bytea.xml is included BEFORE this file in db.changelog-master.xml, so on EVERY boot the sequence is: -8 (re)creates the view, owned by nexus_admin (the migration role) → grants-nexus-diag-1 skips (view already exists, so the legacy branch never fires) → grants-nexus-diag-2's per-relation REVOKE loop (over every relation nexus_admin OWNS) strips SELECT on the view -8 just (re)granted THIS SAME BOOT, plus every base table (never granted in the view era to begin with, since -1 skipped). Measured (nexus-lhuhe, fork rehearsal against a full v0.1.78 walk): nexus_diag ends every boot holding ZERO content-boundary grants — permission denied on the view itself AND on its underlying tables — degrading nx doctor's chash-poison check, the forensics topic, and any post-deploy census to permanently unusable. taxonomy-011-8's own conditional GRANT was never wrong on its own terms; the bug is that BOTH -8 and -1/-2 each assumed the other owned the diag grants' final state, and post-migration neither did.
THE FIX: since this changeset runs LAST among the runAlways grants blocks (this file is included last in db.changelog-master.xml, and -3 is the last changeset in this file), it is the correct place to make the content-boundary grants stick as the final word every boot — re-granting exactly what security_invoker=true requires: SELECT on the view itself, PLUS direct SELECT on every table the view reads internally (security_invoker means Postgres checks the INVOKING role's OWN table privileges for the relations the view references — nexus_diag's BYPASSRLS exempts it from row-level policies, never from ordinary GRANT-based privilege checks). The five tables below are exactly CHASH_BEARING_TABLES (src/nexus/db/chash_tables.py) — the SAME set diag_conformance_view_ddl() reads to build the view text — named individually (never a schema-wide bulk grant) so this stays scoped to precisely what the view needs and does not silently re-widen -2's own content boundary. No mechanical coupling exists between this XML list and the Python tuple (a static changelog cannot import it); a future drift is a manual-review debt, caught by GrantsNexusDiagViewAccessIntegrationTest, which connects AS nexus_diag and SELECTs the view plus every underlying table against a live install.
No foreign-owner guard is needed for the five table grants (unlike the view's own GRANT below): nexus_admin created every one of them via forward DDL and always owns them, the same assumption -1's own unguarded bulk grant already makes for this schema. The view CAN be foreign-owned (a pre-existing superuser-owned copy from pg_provision that taxonomy-011-8's own CREATE OR REPLACE gracefully skipped) — same degrade as taxonomy-011-8's own GRANT: skip with a NOTICE, since that owner's own provisioning path already grants nexus_diag directly.
